title: Top TVs: 4K & OLED for Every Budget (2026)
summary: Tom's Guide and TechRadar both back the LG C6 and LG C5 OLEDs as top all-rounders, the Samsung S95H (S99H) for bright rooms, the Samsung S90F for gaming and the TCL QM8L mini-LED for big screens and sport.
method: Picks come from Tom's Guide's best TVs list (updated Oct 13, 2026) and TechRadar's best TVs guide (updated Oct 8, 2026). Each TV here is named by both sites.
assumptions: Prices are what the retailer price boxes on those pages showed on the day we checked, for the size noted, and they change often. Check the current price on Amazon. Each site tests with its own methods, so brightness and input lag numbers are not directly comparable between them.

products.name: LG C6 OLED
why: TechRadar's top TV and a clear step up from the C5: about 250 nits brighter in its 10% window test, with a quicker processor and vivid, punchy color. Tom's Guide calls it an incredible TV in pretty much every way.
Tom's Guide's only complaint is the launch price, and says it will become one of the best TVs you can buy once it drops. TechRadar's price box now shows a big discount.
specs: Dolby Vision, HDR10 and HLG (no HDR10+)
9.2ms input lag; 1,438 nits peak in TechRadar's Filmmaker mode test
cons: Glossy screen shows reflections in bright rooms
products.best_for: Anyone who wants one TV for movies, sport and gaming
products.skip_if: You mostly watch in a bright, sunny room

products.name: LG C5 OLED
why: TechRadar calls it the ultimate all-rounder, with accurate, punchy color and deep blacks. Tom's Guide ranked it best TV overall for the first half of 2026 and says it now offers incredible performance for the money after price drops.
Tom's Guide says the newer LG B6 only just beat it, and the C5 is cheaper right now.
specs: 144Hz; all four HDMI ports support 4K 144Hz, Dolby Vision gaming, FreeSync and G-Sync
cons: Only a small upgrade over the C4
products.best_for: Buyers who want a top OLED without paying the newest-model price
products.skip_if: You need HDR10+ or an anti-glare screen
products.amazon_listing: LG 65-Inch OLED evo AI 4K C5 Series Smart TV (OLED65C5PUA, 2025)

products.name: Samsung S90F OLED
why: Tom's Guide's best TV for PC and console gaming, with near-perfect contrast, strong color accuracy and Samsung's Game Hub. TechRadar lists it as a solid alternative to the C5 with slightly higher brightness and arguably better gaming features.
Tom's Guide notes the 42 and 48-inch versions use a different panel and are less bright. TechRadar says only the 65-inch size is confirmed as QD-OLED.
specs: 120Hz native, up to 144Hz; four HDMI 2.1 ports
Tizen OS 9, upgradable to Tizen OS 10
HDR10, HDR10+ and HLG (no Dolby Vision)
products.best_for: Gamers who want a high-refresh OLED
products.amazon_listing: Samsung 65-Inch Class OLED S90F 4K Smart TV (2025 Model) NQ4 AI Gen3 Processor Upscaling P

products.name: TCL QM8L
products.badge: Best for sport and big screens
why: Tom's Guide's best TV for live sport and TechRadar's best cheap big-screen pick. Both praise its brightness, deep blacks with little blooming and strong color, and Tom's Guide credits its 144Hz refresh rate for fast motion.
It runs Google TV, which Tom's Guide found quick and easy to use, though both note the Gemini features feel limited.
specs: Google TV; Dolby Vision IQ and HDR10+ support
cons: Color accuracy could be better out of the box
products.best_for: Big living rooms and sports fans who want brightness
products.skip_if: You want the most accurate color or the lowest price
products.amazon_listing: TCL 75 Inch QM8L Series SQD-Mini LED QLED 4K Smart Google TV 75QM8L, 144Hz | 2026, Google

products.name: Samsung S95F OLED
why: TechRadar's pick for bright rooms: vivid colors, high brightness and a glare-free screen that beats reflections. Tom's Guide says it is better than the S90F in most ways but costs far more for fairly minor gains.
TechRadar notes some black crush and slightly raised blacks from the anti-reflection coating.
specs: HDR10, HDR10+ and HLG (no Dolby Vision)
products.best_for: Sunny living rooms where you still want OLED contrast
products.skip_if: You mostly watch in a dark room or want to spend less
products.amazon_listing: Samsung 65-Inch Class OLED S95F 4K Glare Free Smart TV (2025 Model) NQ4 AI Gen3 Processor,

products.name: LG G5 OLED
why: TechRadar's best premium OLED, with a four-stack Primary Tandem RGB panel that hit 2,268 nits in Filmmaker mode, then its brightest OLED test. Tom's Guide says it may be one of the best OLEDs ever made.
Tom's Guide still prefers the cheaper LG B6 unless you need one of the brightest TVs it has tested, and TechRadar notes the C5 delivers similar features for much less.
specs: Dolby Vision, HDR10 and HLG (no HDR10+)
9.1ms input lag with Boost mode on
cons: No input select button on the remote
products.best_for: Wall-mounting and bright rooms when you want a top LG panel
products.skip_if: Value matters more than the last bit of brightness
products.amazon_listing: LG 65-Inch OLED evo AI 4K G5 Series Smart TV (OLED65G5WUA, 2025) | Super Upscaling, Dolby

products.name: LG B5 OLED
why: TechRadar's best budget OLED, with vibrant, accurate color, strong contrast and a very low 9.1ms input lag. It is the cheapest way to get an OLED with four HDMI 2.1 ports.
Tom's Guide says the newer LG B6 is a significant step up in performance and still recommends it over the B5, even though the B5 is slightly cheaper now.
specs: Dolby Vision, HDR10 and HLG (no HDR10+)
668 nits peak brightness in TechRadar's test
products.best_for: Dim to moderately lit rooms on a tighter budget
products.skip_if: You can stretch to the LG B6 or C5, or want a bright-room TV
